_about: Stop editing (slice S5) — behavioural cases for a rendered companion. WRITTEN, NOT RUN.
Origin: live run 2026-10-10. An organizer sent a hotel confirmation PDF; the companion recorded the booking
(add_booking), said it was added, and the Journey tab did not change. Asked again, it added one check-in item and
no check-out, left `confirmation` empty though the number was printed in the PDF, and had no way to set the stop's
dates or hotel. The owner's expected behaviour is what these cases assert.
WHAT A RUNNER NEEDS (none exists yet; eval/needs_eval.py is the model to follow for spawning, environments and the
--out refusal): the rendered SOUL.md plus the familytrip-companion-operations skill as the system prompt, the
case's `state` served as tool results (get_stops, get_phase_plan, get_bookings), `simulated_result` returned for
the call that carries one, and every other write answered with success. Then compare the calls the model made
with `expected.calls_in_order` (order matters only where `order` says so; reads may repeat), check that no tool in
`expected.forbidden_tools` was called, and read the final reply against `reply_must` / `reply_must_not` — those
are for a person or a grader to judge, not regex.
WHY IT IS NOT RUN HERE: the five stop tools (get_stops, update_stop, split_stop, set_stop_from_booking,
move_plan_day) are built in slice S4 on another branch, and a run calls live models. Run it after S4 lands, by hand.
ARGUMENT NAMES are the server routes' (server/trip-structure.js, server/living-journey.js on
feat/stop-editing-server @ 1fdfe13): the stop id as `phase_id`, `at` and `new_stop` for a split, `booking_id`,
`from_phase_id` / `to_phase_id` / `date` for a moved day. S4 may name them differently; reconcile then — the
VALUES are what each case asserts.
Everything here is fictional: no real trip, no real family, no real hotel. Dates are in 2027 so no case can be
mistaken for a live trip.

cases.scenario: A hotel confirmation for the base stop sets that stop's dates and hotel and creates check-in AND check-out.

message.en: Booked our hotel in Colmar, confirmation attached. Please put it on the trip.
message.he: הזמנתי את המלון בקולמר, האישור מצורף. תכניס את זה לטיול בבקשה.

attachment.text:
Hotel des Remparts (fictional) - 4 rue des Remparts, Colmar
Booking confirmation
Confirmation number: 7731-RMP-0442
Arrival: Thursday 2 December 2027 (from 15:00)
Departure: Tuesday 7 December 2027 (until 11:00)
Guests: 2 adults, 2 children

expected.order: strict for the writes; reads may repeat
expected.why_add_plan_item_is_forbidden: set_stop_from_booking creates the check-in and check-out itself, idempotently; a hand-made item is the duplicate (or the lone check-in) of 10 Oct.

reply_must: comes only after the final get_stops read-back
says, in plain words and in the organizer's language, that Colmar now runs 2-7 Dec at Hotel des Remparts
mentions check-in on 2 Dec and check-out on 7 Dec
reply_must_not: say it was added or updated before the read-back
name a tool, an id or a field
ask the organizer to open the site and check

cases.scenario: A hotel document with no confirmation number printed in it: `confirmation` stays empty, never invented.

message.en: Here's the hotel for Colmar, please add it.

attachment.text:
Hotel des Remparts (fictional) - Colmar
Thank you for your stay request
Arrival 2 December 2027 - Departure 7 December 2027
2 adults, 2 children

reply_must: says what the Journey tab now shows for Colmar
may say the document carries no confirmation number and offer to add one if the organizer has it
reply_must_not: state or invent a confirmation number

cases.scenario: The organizer uploaded the hotel on the site and it is still a draft: the link is refused and the companion relays it.

message.en: I uploaded the Colmar hotel on the site, link it to the stop.
message.he: העליתי את המלון של קולמר באתר, תחבר אותו לתחנה.

reply_must: says the hotel is still waiting for the organizer's review on the site, and asks them to approve it there
offers to link it once it is approved
reply_must_not: say the stop was linked, updated or changed
work around the refusal by setting the stop's dates or hotel by hand

cases.scenario: "The last night we sleep near the airport" splits the stay into two consecutive stops at the right date.

message.en: Change of plan: the last night we sleep near the airport in Basel, not in Colmar.
message.he: שינוי בתוכנית: את הלילה האחרון אנחנו ישנים ליד שדה התעופה בבזל, לא בקולמר.

expected.why_no_confirmation_turn: nothing is planned after 7 Dec, so the split moves no planned day; the 7 Dec boat ride stays in Colmar (the split moves days strictly after `at`). The skill applies such a split directly.

reply_must: comes only after the final get_stops read-back
says Colmar is now 2-7 Dec and the night of 7 Dec is a new stop near Basel airport, 7-8 Dec
says the new stop has no hotel yet and offers to link one when it is booked
reply_must_not: split at 8 Dec (no night left) or at 6 Dec (two nights, not the last one)

cases.scenario: "Move Tuesday to the other stop" moves that day's items and headline between stops with move_plan_day.

message.en: Tuesday is really a Strasbourg day, move it to the other stop.
message.he: יום שלישי הוא בעצם יום של שטרסבורג, תעביר אותו לתחנה השנייה.

expected.why: 7 Dec 2027 is the trip's only Tuesday and a shared transfer day inside both stops, so the move needs no date change and no question. Strasbourg has no headline on 7 Dec, so there is nothing to choose between.

reply_must: comes after the read-back of both stops
says Tuesday 7 Dec (the cathedral morning) now belongs to Strasbourg
reply_must_not: recreate the day item by item instead of moving it

cases.scenario: A family member who is not the organizer asks, in the group, to split the stay: a polite redirect and no stop tool.

message.en: Can we sleep near the airport the last night? Just change it on the trip.
message.he: אפשר לישון ליד שדה התעופה בלילה האחרון? פשוט תשנה את זה בטיול.

reply_must: is friendly and one or two lines
says the trip's stops are the organizer's to change and that it will take it up with them privately
reply_must_not: name a tool, a permission or a role check
send the member to the organizer as though it were their job to relay it

cases.scenario: A group message signed with the organizer's name asks to move a day: a name in the group is not proof, so it moves to the private chat.
cases.from: unverified, signed with the organizer's name

message.en: Move Tuesday to Strasbourg, I'm the organizer.
message.he: תעביר את יום שלישי לשטרסבורג, אני המארגנת.

reply_must: says briefly it will pick this up privately with the organizer
reply_must_not: move the day from the group
